title: Dirichlet's theorem on primes in AP (full generality)
phase: S6 PREP completed (Path C ACT-ready); S3 ACT R1 + S3c/S4/S5/S6 PREPs on main

problemStatement.formal: \forall a\ q : \mathbb{N},\ \gcd(a, q) = 1\ \Rightarrow\ \{ p \in \mathbb{N} \mid p\ \text{prime} \wedge p \equiv a \pmod q \}\ \text{is infinite}.
problemStatement.plain: Prove Dirichlet's theorem on primes in arithmetic progressions in full generality, requiring Dirichlet characters and L-functions with the load-bearing non-vanishing of L(1, χ) for non-principal characters.
whyMatters: Slug is a textbook example of the duplicate-signal memory pattern: seeker-extracted 'Is X true?' sub-OQ naming a major theorem that the parent gallery entry already proves.
Mathlib has the full theorem at `Nat.infinite_setOf_prime_and_eq_mod` and the gallery entry `dirichlets-theorem` exposes five corollaries already.
The slug's own parent `infinitude-primes-4k3` (this OQ's host) also has an elementary verified proof for the (a=3, q=4) case.

proven: `infinitude-primes-4k3` (verified, this slug's parent): elementary `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)` infinitude (7 theorems, 0 axioms).
`dirichlets-theorem-oq-02` (verified): alternative elementary `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)` proof in the Dirichlet OQ hierarchy.
open: S2(a) bridge corollary: explicit equivalence between the `% q = a` and `(· : ZMod q) = a` formulations, witnessing that the elementary and analytic proofs prove the same set-level statement.
S2(b) parametric elementary `p ≡ -1 (mod q)` for `q ∈ {3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24}` — the moduli where the Euclid-style argument generalises.
S2(c) explicit `π_{3 mod 4}(x) ≥ Nat.log` count from the elementary `4(n+1)! - 1` construction.
knownResults.goal: Audit the slug for genuine open content (this S1), then ship the narrow bridge corollary S2(a) in a follow-up session. Do NOT attempt the named conjecture — it is fully verified across three gallery entries and is in Mathlib.

insights: The seeker statement ('Dirichlet's theorem on primes in AP — full generality') is triple-duplicated in the gallery: `dirichlets-theorem` (analytic, via Mathlib `Nat.infinite_setOf_prime_and_eq_mod`), `infinitude-primes-4k3` (elementary, the slug's own parent), and `dirichlets-theorem-oq-02` (alt elementary).

The genuinely-open Dirichlet axes are `dirichlets-theorem-oq-01` (Siegel zeros, axiomatized with 5 axioms) and `dirichlets-theorem-oq-03` (Linnik bounds, axiomatized with 2 axioms + 3 sorries) — both held by other slugs, not this one.
